title: Call spec sanitizer and actionable error hints for JSON parameter validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight 'call spec sanitizer' pipeline inside the runtime that validates function/tool call payloads against a compact JSON schema format and returns human-actionable, example-driven error hints rather than opaque schema failures. This ticket defines the schema shape we will accept as the canonical runtime input, the permissive sanitizer modes (strict, suggest, tolerant), the error hint taxonomy, and the telemetry events needed to track validation regressions and assist customer debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts canonical call-spec envelope containing name, version, params (JSON) and metadata; envelope schema documented in runtime README
Sanitizer supports three modes: strict (reject on first violation), suggest (return normalized params + hints), tolerant (attempt best-effort coercion + record hints)
Error responses include an error_code, user_facing_message, suggestion_snippets (example corrected JSON fragments), and a single-line debug_hint for logs
SDKs (js/py/go) map sanitizer error responses to typed exceptions with fields: code, path, suggestion, docs_url
Telemetry events emitted for: validation_failure, auto_correction_applied, schema_mismatch_rate per model-route
Automated tests cover 50+ variants: missing keys, type mismatches, enum failures, nested arrays, unknown fields, and ambiguous coercions
decisions: Adopt a compact JSON schema subset instead of full JSON Schema draft to keep runtime parsing cheap and deterministic
Expose three sanitizer modes as a per-route configuration in runtime config so customers can opt into permissive behavior during rollout
Return suggested minimal diffs (not whole object replacements) in suggestion_snippets to minimize bandwidth and make fixes copy-pasteable
Do not attempt semantic repairs (e.g., mapping 'priority: high' -> 3) — only syntactic/structural corrections (type casts, default injection, trimming)
implementation_notes: Sanitizer implemented as a middleware in serving runtime; runs after tokenization and before model dispatch
Use hand-written validator for the compact schema to avoid unpredictable behavior of full-featured JSON Schema libs under load
Normalization rules: string->number when numeric string detected, boolean coercion for 'true'/'false' strings, trim long strings to config.max_param_length with warning
Provide a small 'repair' module that produces suggestion_snippets and an ordered list of applied fixes for telemetry
Integrate with existing parameter-telemetry pipeline: include validation code and sanitized_hash in normal per-request spans
testing_plan: Unit tests for validator core covering positive and negative cases
Property tests fuzzing malformed user inputs to ensure sanitizer never panics and never mutates request in strict mode
Integration tests with SDK sample apps exercising suggest and tolerant modes
Performance benchmark: measure median latency regression < 0.4ms at p95 under 1000 rps with sanitizer enabled
Run canary for 2 days on a subset of traffic routing to suggest mode and measure correction acceptance metric
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy sanitizer in suggest mode for internal routes and opt-in customers. Phase 2: enable for low-risk public routes (warn-only). Phase 3: offer strict mode for enterprise tenants and use as default for new routes after 4 weeks of observation.
